toegepas.rede_vinder: 'Laastens' marks the third of four steps, so the sequence eers-dan-laastens-dan reads out of order; 'daarna' keeps the order without repeating 'dan'.
toegepas.fout: 'Laastens' marks the third step while a further step ('Sê dan') follows, so the sequence eers-dan-laastens-dan reads out of order.
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'Daarna' keeps the same actions in the same order and removes the false 'last'; it must go in together with change 2.

toegepas.voor: Sê dan in jou eie woorde
toegepas.na: Sê laastens in jou eie woorde
toegepas.rede_vinder: Moves 'laastens' to the step that is actually last, paired with the change to the previous sentence.
toegepas.fout: 'Dan' after 'laastens' adds a step after the one called last.
toegepas.rede_keurder: Putting 'laastens' on the step that is actually last makes the sequence read correctly without changing any action, and it pairs with change 1.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: 'n Vlermuis is nie 'n voël nie maar 'n dier
laat_vaar_vorige.na: 'n Vlermuis is nie 'n voël nie, maar 'n dier
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A comma before 'maar' after the closing 'nie' marks the contrast and makes the sentence easier to read.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'maar 'n dier met vlerke van vel' has no verb of its own, so the AWS rule for a comma joining two sentences does not apply, and the double 'nie' already marks the contrast clearly.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: omdat mense hulle gebou het met dele wat soos 'n masjien saamwerk
laat_vaar_vorige.na: omdat mense hulle met dele gebou het wat soos 'n masjien saamwerk
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: In a subordinate clause the verb cluster normally goes after the prepositional phrase.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Putting the prepositional phrase after 'gebou het' is normal, natural Afrikaans and keeps 'dele' next to its relative clause; the proposal is only a different word order, and it matches the wording of the 'meganies' glossary entry less closely.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Sit 'n natuurlike vlerk langs 'n meganiese een.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Sit 'n natuurlike en 'n meganiese vlerk langs mekaar.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'n meganiese een' copies English 'a mechanical one'; Afrikaans does not use 'een' as a noun substitute this way.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Using 'een' as a noun substitute ('n meganiese een') is ordinary Afrikaans, so the proposal is a lateral rewording.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Jou eie werk en 'n maat se werk
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Kyk met dieselfde stappe na jou eie prent of model van iets wat vlieg.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Gebruik dieselfde stappe om na jou eie prent of model van iets wat vlieg te kyk.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: One does not look 'with' steps; using the steps to look reads more naturally and keeps the meaning.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original is clear to a Grade 5 reader, while the proposal is longer, puts a long object between 'na' and 'te kyk', breaks the parallel with 'Kyk net so na' in the next sentence and repeats 'Gebruik' from the paragraph's last sentence.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Jy kyk net na hoe hulle lyk en nie na hoe hulle vlieg nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Jy kyk net na hoe hulle lyk, nie na hoe hulle vlieg nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The contrast reads more naturally without the joining 'en'; meaning unchanged.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original 'en nie na' is natural Afrikaans; replacing it with a comma is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.na: Aan die agterkant en by die punt
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A bare 'Agter' opening the sentence is terse and vague; 'aan die agterkant' says plainly that it is the back edge of the wing.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Agter' reads clearly against 'Die voorste rand' in the sentence before, so the longer phrase is a lateral move.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The subject is the colour, and colour does not 'have' spots or stripes; it forms them, which keeps the meaning and the 'kan'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Kleur kan kolle of strepe he' is acceptable, and the verb 'vorm' would sit two sentences after the art term 'vorm' (shape) in a lesson that teaches that term, which could confuse a reader.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: omdat die groot vere daar een vir een eindig
laat_vaar_vorige.na: omdat elke groot veer daar apart eindig
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'een vir een' suggests a sequence in time; the point is that each feather ends separately, which makes the edge uneven.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'een vir een eindig' is natural Afrikaans and here plainly means the feathers end one after another along the edge; the proposal is a lateral move and reads stiffer.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: sit in sy vere en kan kolle of strepe hê
laat_vaar_vorige.na: sit in sy vere, wat kolle of strepe kan hê
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As written, the subject of 'kan kolle of strepe hê' is the colour itself; tying it to the feathers reads more naturally and keeps the protected opening intact.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The original reads acceptably with colour (the art element the block is about) as the subject; the proposal shifts the subject to the feathers and adds a relative clause without being clearly better for a Grade 5 reader.

laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'vassit' is the natural Afrikaans verb for parts attached to something; 'vas is' is stiffer.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'waaraan die vlerke vas is' is correct, natural Afrikaans, so this is a lateral move, and it would also reword a glossary definition, which only the writer may do.
